lesson.text: Remember? A noun names a thing and a verb is a doing word. Describing words make them come alive.
Adjectives describe nouns: a tall tree, a fluffy cat, three green frogs. They tell what kind, what colour, what size or how many.
Adverbs describe verbs: they tell how, when or where. The snail moved slowly. We played outside. Many adverbs end in -ly: quickly, softly, happily.
Compare two things with -er: Zara's tower is taller than Bram's. Compare three or more with -est: Mimi's tower is the tallest of all.
Watch the spelling: big, bigger, biggest (double the g). Happy, happier, happiest (y becomes i). Nice, nicer, nicest (just add r or st).
Long adjectives use more and most: more beautiful, the most beautiful. Some are irregular: good, better, best; bad, worse, worst.
Try it in the world: build three towers and describe them: tall, taller, the tallest. Then say how your buddy moved, with an adverb: slowly, quickly, happily. Next: joining sentences.

exercises.prompt: Which word is an adjective in "a fluffy cat"?
exercises.hint: Which word describes the cat?
exercises.explain: Fluffy describes the cat, so it is an adjective.

exercises.prompt: Which word is an adverb in "The snail moved slowly"?
exercises.hint: Which word tells how it moved?
exercises.explain: Slowly tells how the snail moved: it is an adverb.

exercises.prompt: Zara's tower is ___ than Bram's.
exercises.hint: Comparing two things: add -er.
exercises.explain: Comparing two towers: taller.

exercises.prompt: An adjective describes a noun.
exercises.hint: Think of a tall tree.
exercises.explain: True: tall describes the tree.

exercises.prompt: Which is the biggest? The mouse is small, the cat is big, the horse is the ___.
exercises.hint: Short word, one vowel, one consonant: double it.
exercises.explain: Double the g and add -est: biggest.

exercises.prompt: Which word describes how Pip sang? "Pip sang happily."
exercises.hint: How did he sing?
exercises.explain: Happily tells how Pip sang: it is an adverb.

exercises.prompt: This is the ___ day of my life!
exercises.hint: happy: change y to i.
exercises.explain: Change y to i and add -est: happiest.

exercises.prompt: Which one is an adverb that tells where?
exercises.hint: Where did we play?
exercises.explain: Outside tells where; quickly tells how and yesterday tells when.

exercises.prompt: "Gooder" is the right way to compare two things with "good".
exercises.hint: good is irregular.
exercises.explain: False: good, better, best.

exercises.prompt: The rainbow was the ___ thing I had ever seen.
exercises.hint: Long adjectives use more or most.
exercises.explain: Beautiful is long, so we say the most beautiful.

exercises.prompt: My cold is ___ today than yesterday.
exercises.hint: Is your cold getting better or getting more unwell? Which comparing word fits bad?
exercises.explain: Comparing two days: worse.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order, from the least to the most.
exercises.hint: Which one compares the most?
exercises.explain: Good, better, best: each is more than the one before.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses an adjective AND an adverb?
exercises.hint: Find a word for the mouse and a word for how it ran.
exercises.explain: Tiny describes the mouse (adjective); quickly describes how it ran (adverb).

exercises.prompt: Of the three towers, Mimi's is the ___.
exercises.hint: Three or more things: add -est.
exercises.explain: Comparing three towers: tallest.

exercises.prompt: "More faster" is correct.
exercises.hint: Use -er or more, never both.
exercises.explain: False: say faster, not more faster.

exercises.prompt: Sort the words: adjective or adverb?
exercises.hint: Does it describe a thing or how something is done?
exercises.explain: Adjectives: fluffy, tall. Adverbs: slowly, quietly.

exercises.prompt: Match each adjective to its -est word.
exercises.hint: Two of them are irregular, and the long one uses most.
exercises.explain: Good, best; bad, worst; beautiful, the most beautiful.

exercises.prompt: Sort the adverbs: do they tell how, when or where?
exercises.hint: Ask: does it tell how something is done, when it happens, or where?
exercises.explain: How: slowly, happily. When: yesterday, soon. Where: outside, upstairs.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its -er word for comparing two things.
exercises.hint: Remember the spelling rules: double the last letter, y to i, just add r, or a new word.
exercises.explain: Big, bigger (double the g). Happy, happier (y becomes i). Nice, nicer (just add r). Bad, worse (a new word).

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: is the comparing word right?
items: Mimi's tower is the tallest of all.
My kite is more faster than yours.
This is the happiest day ever.
Zara's cake is bigger than Bram's.
exercises.hint: Two things take -er; three or more take -est. Watch for words that change.
exercises.explain: Right: the tallest of all, the happiest day, bigger than Bram's. Not right: say faster, not more faster; and say the worst storm, not the baddest.
